To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the non-neutralizing antibody levels against VP1 in EVs and rhinoviruses in infants and children in Shanghai are high in the neonatal age group, low in the 1-12 month age group, high in the 13-60 month age group and low in the 61-72 month age group.
the overall non-neutralized antibody responses against VP-1 of the EV- A, B, and RV-A viruses were detected among infants and children in Shanghai.
the anti-VP1 antibody responses in infants and children were age-dependent and the anti-RV13 antibody responses were the highest, followed by anti-CB3, PV1, CA16 and EV71.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the anti-VP1 antibody responses against EVs among infants and children in Shanghai.
the overall non-neutralising antibody response against VP1 in the EV-A, EV-B, EV-C and RV-A species among infants and children in Shanghai.
the non-neutralizing antibody response against EV infections among children, and the results could be helpful to further understanding the ubiquitous nature of EV infections among children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the overall non-neutralization antibody responses against the VP1 of EVs and RVs are age-dependent and species-specific among infants and children in Shanghai.

the non-neutralizing antibody reactivity against VP1 of all EV species and RV-A species in the infants and children in Shanghai was detected and the anti-VP1 antibody levels were in an age-related pattern.
the non-neutralizing antibody response against VP1 is age-dependent, virus-dependent and species-dependent among infants and children in Shanghai.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the overall non-neutralization antibody response against VP1 of four major species of EVs (A, B, C, and RV-A) among infants and children in Shanghai is characterized by a high level in the first month, the lowest level in 1–12 months, the peak level in 13–60 months, and the lowest level again in 61–72 months.
the anti-VP1 antibody levels against these EVs were age-dependent, with a peak level in 13–60 months, and the anti-RV13 antibodies were at the highest level.

we have developed a novel evolved immunoglobin-binding molecule (NEIBMs)-based ELISA to detect the overall non-neutralization antibody response against VP1 of four EVs and one RV among infants and children in Shanghai.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the overall non-neutralization antibody response against VP1 among infants and children is age-related and is different among EVs.
the non-neutralizing antibody response against VP1 of RV-A viruses was higher than that of other EV species among the infants and young children.
the non-neutralizing antibody levels against VP1 of different EVs in infants and children are age-related, which could provide a basis for further understanding the overall EV infection in children.
